231953329_132cf2e1.text: Hilar mossy cells (MCs) are large glutamatergic neurons that innervate both GCs and inhibitory GABAergic neurons within the DG (Scharfman, 2016)(Scharfman et al., 2013). MCs make up the majority of hilar neurons, and are known for their complex spines called thorny excrescences (Scharfman, 2016)(Scharfman et al., 2013). They have dendrites mainly in the hilus and their axon projects to locations within the DG. Near the cell body the axon makes collaterals that terminate mainly in the hilus. Distal to the cell body the axon terminates at many septotemporal levels. There is also a commissural projection that terminates in the contralateral DG (Scharfman et al., 2013)

231953329_6e82fb76.text: Mossy cells are large glutamatergic neurons located in the dentate hilus and represent a major cell type that innervates both granule cells and local GABAergic interneurons (Scharfman et al., 2015)(Botterill et al., 2021). These cells are the principal and only glutamatergic neurons in the dentate hilus (Sun et al., 2017).

231953329_4507515d.text: The most distinctive morphological feature of mossy cells is their characteristic thorny excrescences - complex spines that encrust their proximal dendrites and give them a 'mossy' appearance (Botterill et al., 2021)(Fredes et al., 2021)(Sun et al., 2017).

231953329_e5431c02.text: Their axons make local collaterals near the cell body that terminate in the hilus, but the majority of their axonal projections extend distally to terminate in the inner molecular layer of the dentate gyrus across multiple septotemporal levels (Botterill et al., 2021)(Fredes et al., 2021). Additionally, mossy cells have commissural projections that terminate in the contralateral dentate gyrus (Botterill et al., 2021).
